summary: Hyoung Seok Ham works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Virginia in 2010 and earned a PhD from the University of Michigan (attested 2016) under Madhav M. Deshpande, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and others.

Hywel David Lewis (1910–1992) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Ysgol Syr Hugh Owen, Bangor University (circa 1928–1932), and Jesus College, Oxford (circa 1932–1936), he held a post at Bangor University (circa 1936–1955).

Hürelbaatar Ujeed specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge, he held posts at Cambridge (attested 2010) and Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

Ian Charles Harris (1952–2014) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Cambridge and Lancaster University (PhD 1985). He held posts at Lancaster, St Hugh's College, Oxford, NUS, and Cumbria, where he became Professor Emeritus.

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University in 2004 and served as a research fellow at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute (attested 2005).
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka, later teaching Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.

Ian Reader (born 1949) is a Japanology and religious studies scholar. After earning his doctorate from the University of Leeds (circa 1979–1983), he held posts at Kansai Gaidai, Stirling, Hawaiʻi, Lancaster, and Manchester (circa 2006–2015).

Ibrahim Shah is a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He earned a PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar in 2007 under Muhammad Farooq Swati and others, and became an Associate Professor and Department Chairman at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa (born 1936) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (circa 1955–1959) and held posts at Otani University Junior College (attested 1978) and Otani University (circa 1967–2001).

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) studied religious studies and archaeology at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Nishogakusha, Kokugakuin, Tohoku, and Seijo universities, and at the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama (born 1942) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa and Otani universities under Kogen Mizuno, and served as a professor at Komazawa University from 1985 to 2013, among other visiting and leadership roles.

Ichiro Numata is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and Indology. He holds part-time lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the Sapienza University of Rome, where he later served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (circa 1935–1940) and held posts at Pravda, the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, and the Institute of Oriental Studies (circa 1960–1998).

Ihsan Ali (born 1955) works in archaeology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin, he served as Director of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Archaeology, Professor at Peshawar, and Vice Chancellor of Hazara University.

Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Komazawa University. His studies were conducted under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.

Ikuhisa Takigawa (born 1968) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University, he has held posts as a part-time lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University (both attested 2002).

Ikuko Tazaki specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She has held research posts at Otani University as a special researcher and at Kyoto University's Center for Southeast Asian Studies as an affiliated researcher (both attested 2017).

Ikuro Hattori specializes in Indology and philosophy. He holds a PhD from Pune University and has held posts at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2003), Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026), and Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2026).

Ilkka Pyysiäinen (born 1959) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under Juha Pentikäinen, René Gothóni, and Simo Knuuttila, and has held posts at the University of Helsinki (from 1984) and the University of Oxford.
